title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: A research-and-teaching pathway focused on corporate governance, company law, competition regulation, securities markets, financial regulation and related public-policy questions.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes the student is pursuing or beginning this Ph.D. in 2026. Faculty recruitment and promotion timelines vary by institution, so the sequence below is indicative rather than a guaranteed timetable.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Establish a strong research identity in corporate, competition or securities law, publish peer-reviewed work and build teaching evidence.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop a distinct research programme, pursue postdoctoral/research opportunities where useful and become competitive for faculty positions.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Become an independent scholar, doctoral supervisor and research-grant applicant with a sustained publication record.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine scholarship, teaching, doctoral supervision, policy engagement and academic leadership as financial and regulatory systems evolve.

blocks.label: Career progression
blocks.text: Ph.D. Researcher (2026–2030±) → Postdoctoral Researcher / Research Fellow (2030–2033±) → Assistant Professor (2030s) → Associate Professor (mid/late 2030s) → Professor (late 2030s–2040s) → Senior Professor / Chair → Centre Director / Dean
PhD/postdoctoral research routes

A senior professor in this field should increasingly combine scholarship with institution-building. A strong profile could include doctoral supervision, major research projects, books and journal publications, international collaborations, policy consultation, executive education and leadership of a corporate/competition/securities-law research centre. The research agenda should continue adapting to digital markets, AI, fintech, sustainable finance and changing capital-market regulation.
